descriptionChirho: A twisted cord or string used for binding, fastening, or tying objects together. Used of the blue cord (פְּתִיל תְּכֵלֶת) attached to the priestly breastpiece (Exodus 28:28, 28:37, 39:21, 39:31), the cord securing a vessel lid (Numbers 19:15), the cord and signet ring given as a pledge by Judah to Tamar (Genesis 38:18, 38:25), and the cord in Ezekiel 40:3. Multilingual glosses: Arabic خَيْط 'thread/string,' German Schnur 'cord,' French cordon 'cord,' Spanish cordon/cordel 'cord,' Korean 끈 'string,' Hindi डोरी 'cord.' Includes both singular and plural forms (פְּתִילִם in Exodus 39:3, gold threads woven into the ephod).

A thin strand or filament, distinguished from the thicker 'cord' sense by its use in contexts emphasizing thinness, fragility, or fine textile work. In Numbers 15:38 the thread of blue (פְּתִיל תְּכֵלֶת) on garment tassels/fringes, and in Judges 16:9 Samson snaps his bonds 'as a thread of tow (פְּתִיל הַנְּעֹרֶת) breaks at the touch of fire,' where the comparison emphasizes the thread's fragility. German Faden 'thread,' French fil 'thread,' Spanish hilo 'thread,' Korean 실 'thread,' Hindi रेशा/धागा 'fiber/thread' -- all distinguishing this from the heavier 'cord' glosses.
